input: grid is a nonempty rectangular R by C array of safe-integer colors with distinct mutable row objects, and R * C is within the shared collection-size bound. row and col designate an in-bounds start cell; color is a safe integer. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: The identical input grid object after changing exactly the border cells of the original-color cardinal component containing (row, col). A component cell is border if it is on the array boundary or has a cardinal neighbor outside the component.
mutation_aliasing: Intentionally mutates only border cell values, returning the exact original outer array. Every row object, array length, non-border cell and external row alias is preserved. All border decisions occur before any recoloring, so equal/new colors cannot change discovery. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Colors are compared and assigned exactly without arithmetic. Coordinates, queue positions and component size are bounded by R * C. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(R * C + R + 1) time and O(R * C + R + 1) auxiliary space, including the visited matrix, retained-head queue and border list. Each component cell is enqueued once; at most four neighbor checks per visit. Input/output grid storage is not newly allocated. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.
